events.what: Kawauchi claims a full proof of the Whitehead aspherical conjecture via ribbon sphere-links (arXiv:2303.04368); v2 April 2024, later published in Journal of Mathematical Techniques and Computational Mathematics (Opast), 2024
events.credibility_reason: Landmark problem; no expert uptake, citation or discussion in over three years; published in a venue the record documents as predatory-looking (Opast); the live Wikipedia article still lists the conjecture as open and does not mention it; only follow-up is the author's own self-referential lemma papers.

events.what: Mikhovich, rational and p-adic analogues of Whitehead's conjecture (Izvestiya 2025; arXiv:2105.00281)
formal-conjectures GitHub issue #2189 cataloguing the conjecture as a formalisation target

judgement.doubts: The arXiv v2 (April 2024) is not shown by the record to contain new mathematics, so the claim dates to March 2023, before the snapshot; even if post-snapshot it would be set aside as not credible. Only the abstract was read by the researcher; no specific error is identified, so it is not knocked_down.

outcome_prefix: Judged: the only event is Kawauchi's March 2023 claimed proof (arXiv:2303.04368), which predates the snapshot and is set aside as not credible, so the conjecture stays open.

corrections.why: F7: the record says v1 was posted March 2023 and gives no sign that the April 2024 v2 contains new mathematics, so the event is the 2023 posting, before the snapshot.

F5/F7: the claim predates the snapshot, and it is not credible anyway. On a landmark problem it has had no expert uptake or citation for over three years, it appeared in the Opast venue that the record flags as predatory, and the live Wikipedia article still calls the conjecture open. Nothing survives, and nothing resolved it before the snapshot, so the status is open, not open_stale.
other: an open status carries a null direction (§4 step 6).
